title: One Thread or Many: Executors, Callback Groups and the Control Loop Stuck Behind the Planner

questions.question: A planner callback takes 50 ms and a control callback runs every 10 ms on the same single thread. What happens to the control loop?
options: It is held up by up to 45 ticks while the planner runs, and a planner of 200 ticks held it up by 195
questions.explanation: The slow callback holds up every other callback on the thread.

questions.question: What does two threads with the control and the planner in separate groups give the control callback?
options: 0: it runs on time, while the planner runs beside it

questions.question: Everything is in one mutually exclusive group and the executor has two threads. What is the worst wait?
options: 45, exactly what one thread gave: callbacks in one exclusive group never overlap, and the second thread sits idle
questions.explanation: More threads do nothing for callbacks that share an exclusive group.

questions.question: What does making the group reentrant cost?
options: The callbacks of that group can now run at once, so whatever they share needs a lock: the race the exclusive group was preventing
questions.explanation: Reentrant moves the burden to the callbacks.

questions.question: Four 10 tick callbacks are ready together in a reentrant group on two threads. When do they start?
options: 0 0 10 10: a group that allows overlap still has only as many threads as there are
questions.explanation: With three threads the third started at once.

questions.question: A callback blocked by its group is ahead of one in another group in the queue. What happens to the second?
options: It runs at once: a blocked callback does not hold up those behind it, and one that never started is reported as having waited the whole time
questions.explanation: Leaving the never started ones out of the measure would say the worst wait was 0.
